| stat3value = 400 (0.8 apg) }} '''Hakim Hanif Warrick''' (born July 8, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A [[power forward]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]] from 2001 to 2005. He won an [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA championship]] in [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2003]] and blocked a potential game-tying three-pointer in the title game. Warrick was selected in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He played for eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the Grizzlies, [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[New Orleans Hornets]] and [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. Warrick then embarked on an international career and played in China, Turkey, Australia, Greece, Puerto Rico, Lebanon and Israel. He played his final season in the [[NBA G League]] during the 2018–19 season. ==High school career== Warrick played for [[Friends' Central School]] in [[Wynnewood, Pennsylvania]]. In his senior season (2000–2001), he helped Friends' Central to a 23–2 record and the Friends Schools League title{{cite web |title=Championships by Sport and Year|url=http://friendsschoolsleague.org/VERT.html|access-date=2011-02-07}} with averages of 15.6 points, 13.0 rebounds and 4.8 blocks. It was Friends' Central's first title since 1974. For his efforts, Warrick earned All-Friends League, All-Mainline and all-state honors.{{cite web |title=Hakim Warrick Profile |url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=552&sport=176&roster=142 |work=SUAthletics.com |access-date=2007-09-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090111013844/http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=552&sport=176&roster=142 |archive-date=2009-01-11 |url-status=dead }} ==College career== Even with his high school's proximity to the [[City 6]], comprising Division I programs [[University of Pennsylvania|Penn]], [[Saint Joseph's University|St. Joseph's]], [[Temple University|Temple]], [[La Salle University|LaSalle]], [[Drexel University|Drexel]], and [[Villanova University|Villanova]], none of those schools heavily recruited Warrick.{{cite web |title=Philly's Finest |first=Tim |last=Gorman |date=2005-02-14 |url=http://www.dailyorange.com/home/index.cfm?event=displayArticle&ustory_id=4f0a629b-8546-49b8-889a-e34259bcd484 |work=The Daily Orange |access-date=2007-09-02 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071109175711/http://www.dailyorange.com/home/index.cfm?event=displayArticle&ustory_id=4f0a629b-8546-49b8-889a-e34259bcd484 |archive-date = 2007-11-09}} Syracuse was not initially high on Warrick, either, as Warrick was considered a last resort by the Syracuse coaching staff and was only offered a scholarship when All-American recruit [[Julius Hodge]] selected [[North Carolina State University|North Carolina State]] over Syracuse.{{cite web |title=Warrick went from rough prospect to superstar |date=2005-03-04 |url=http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/7072306 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050308022606/http://msnbc.msn.com/id/7072306/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2005-03-08 |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-02}}{{cite news |last1=Lieber |first1=Scott |title=Luck of the Orange |url=https://dailyorange.com/2004/11/luck-of-the-orange/ |access-date=8 March 2023 |work=[[The Daily Orange]] |date=8 November 2004}} ===Freshman=== Warrick appeared in all 35 games his freshman year, starting 19-straight games starting with a game against [[Binghamton University|Binghamton]], and remained there until Jan. 28, 2002 against [[Georgetown Hoyas|Georgetown]]. Warrick averaged 6.0 points and 4.3 rebounds and the Orangemen were 15–4 during that stretch. However, Syracuse coach [[Jim Boeheim]] had to promote James Thues to the starting lineup after DeShaun Williams struggled as the team's starting point guard.{{cite web |title=DeShaun Williams Profile |url=http://www.orangehoops.org/DWilliams.htm |work=Orangehooops.org |access-date=2007-09-02}} Although the Orange missed the NCAA Tournament, Warrick played a key role in Syracuse's run to the NIT Final Four. Warrick had 14 points, 10 rebounds and a career-high six blocks in the first-round victory against St. Bonaventure and against Richmond, Warrick had 15 points and 14 rebounds. The Orange lost to Temple in the semifinal round 65–54. Warrick finished with 12 points, going 2-of-12 from the free-throw line, including four key misses in the final minutes of the game.{{cite web |title=Temple vs. Syracuse |date=2002-03-28 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/scores102/102087/102087318.htm |work=Ticker |access-date=2007-09-02}} ===Sophomore=== Warrick started all 35 games in his sophomore year and was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Big East Most Improved Player]] after more than doubling his scoring average from the previous year (6.1 to 14.8 ppg) and improving his rebound average by 3.7 boards per game (4.8 to 8.5 rpg). He was also named to the USBWA All-District II Team and the All-Big East Third Team. Warrick also played a large role in Syracuse's first [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|National Championship]]. In the Sweet 16 against Auburn and the Elite 8 against Oklahoma, Warrick averaged 14.0 points and 6.5 rebounds, and was named to the All-East Regional team. In the semifinal against Texas, he scored 18 points. However, Warrick is best known for his blocked shot in the [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|National Championship]] game against [[Kansas Jayhawks|Kansas]]. Leading by three with under 15 seconds left, Warrick missed two free throws that would've sealed the game with Syracuse hanging on to a three-point lead, 81–78.{{cite web |title=Freshmen Anthony, McNamara lead Boeheim to first title |date=2003-04-07 |url=http://cbs.sportsline.com/collegebasketball/gamecenter/recap/NCAAB_20030407_SYR@KS |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-02}} With 1.5 seconds left and the score still the same, Kansas' Michael Lee was wide-open from the baseline for a potential game-tying 3-pointer. But Warrick used his long arms to block Lee's attempt and Syracuse captured its first ever national championship.{{cite news |title=Warrick's block denies final seconds of deja vu |first=Bruce |last=Feldman |date=2003-04-07 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/ncaatourney04/news/story?id=1737331 |work=[[ESPN The Magazine]] |access-date=2007-09-02 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071109175711/http://www.dailyorange.com/home/index.cfm?event=displayArticle&ustory_id=4f0a629b-8546-49b8-889a-e34259bcd484 |archive-date = 2007-11-09}}{{cite news |last1=Vasudevan |first1=Anish |title=Hakim Warrick was known for 'the block' in 2003. But he was so much more at Syracuse |url=https://dailyorange.com/2023/03/syracuse-mens-basketball-hakim-warrick-jersey-retirement-2003-anniversary/ |access-date=8 March 2023 |work=The Daily Orange |date=6 March 2023}} ====Team USA==== Warrick was one of 16 finalists for the 2003 USA Basketball Men's Pan American Games Team. However, he did not make the cut.{{cite web |title=Warrick Misses Out On Pan American Games |date=2003-07-18 |url=http://www.suathletics.com/News/basketball/mbasket/2003/7/18/WarrickUSA.asp?path=mbasket |work=USA Basketball |access-date=2007-09-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930152329/http://www.suathletics.com/News/basketball/mbasket/2003/7/18/WarrickUSA.asp?path=mbasket |archive-date=2007-09-30 |url-status=dead }} ===Junior=== After [[Carmelo Anthony]] declared early for the NBA draft, Warrick became the team's top scoring option. He led the team in scoring (19.8) and rebounds (8.6), and was named to the second-team All-America teams by ESPN.com and The Sporting News. He was also a finalist for three national player of the year awards – the Naismith, Rupp and Wooden awards and was a first-team All-Big East selection. Syracuse advanced to the Sweet 16 and in the second-round game against [[University of Maryland, College Park|Maryland]], Warrick scored 26 points and added nine rebounds.{{cite web |title=Warrick's 26 carries 'Cuse to Sweet 16 |date=2004-03-20 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=244000037 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915050810/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=244000037 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 15, 2016 |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-02}} Over the three NCAA Tournament games, Warrick averaged 22.3 points and 6.3 rebounds an outing. ===Senior=== Warrick continued his improvement in his final year, averaging 21.4 points and 8.6 rebounds per game. He was named the Big East Conference Player of the Year and was a consensus All-American from the [[Associated Press]], CollegeInsider.com, [[NABC Player of the Year|NABC]], [[Rivals.com]], Rupp Team and Wooden Team. Syracuse captured the 2005 Big East Championship. During those three games, and one game in the NCAA Tournament, Warrick led Syracuse with averages of 22.5 points and 12.0 rebounds. However, Warrick's last game at Syracuse was a disappointment, as fourth-seeded Syracuse was handed a 60–57 overtime upset in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] by 13th seeded [[University of Vermont|Vermont]]. Warrick had 21 points in the defeat.{{cite web |title=Vermont vs. Syracuse |date=2005-03-18 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/scores105/105077/20050318NCAABSYRACUSE--0nr.htm |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-02}} ===College legacy=== Warrick finished his career with averages of 15.4 points on 53.6% shooting, 7.6 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game. He finished second all-time at Syracuse in free throws made (529) and free throws attempted (803), third for consecutive double-figure scoring games (61) and fourth in points (2,073) and rebounds (1,025).{{cite web |title=Grizzlies Select Hakim Warrick with the 19th Pick in the NBA draft |date=2005-06-28 |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_select_hakim_warrick-050628.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=2007-09-02}} Warrick also left Syracuse as one of the most prolific dunkers in the school's history, aided by his 7-foot-1 wingspan.{{cite web |title=Warrick's eye-popping jams defy basketball purists |first=Adam |last=Kilgore |date=2003-11-21 |url=http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2003/11/21/200304BasketballGuide/Warricks.EyePopping.Jams.Defy.Basketball.Purists-565231.shtml |work=The Daily Orange |access-date=2007-09-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071109185929/http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2003/11/21/200304BasketballGuide/Warricks.EyePopping.Jams.Defy.Basketball.Purists-565231.shtml |archive-date=2007-11-09 |url-status=dead }} Specifically, Warrick is known for two dunks. The first came against the [[Texas Longhorns]] in the National Semifinal of the 2003 NCAA tournament. In the second half, Warrick collected a rebound, dribbled once, and leaped over 6-foot-3 [[Royal Ivey]].{{cite web |title=Warrick emulating Anthony for Orangemen |date=2003-03-23 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2004/basketball/ncaa/specials/ncaa_tourney/2004/03/23/phoenix.rdp.ap/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040416095937/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2004/basketball/ncaa/specials/ncaa_tourney/2004/03/23/phoenix.rdp.ap/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 16, 2004 |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-02}} The dunk, which came with Ivey's face buried in Warrick's midsection, was actually scored as an offensive foul. Warrick was impressed at his own feat the following day: "It's one of those things you amaze yourself, you just can't believe you did it."{{cite web |title=Collison has ties to Boeheim |first=Brian |last=Landman |date=2003-04-07 |url=http://www.sptimes.com/2003/04/07/news_pf/Sports/Collison_has_ties_to_.shtml |work=St. Petersburg Times |access-date=2007-09-02}} The second came against Notre Dame on January 10, 2005, in Warrick's senior year. With 17:15 left in the first half, Warrick took an entry pass from [[Gerry McNamara]] in the left block, about six feet from the hoop. Warrick was met in the lane by Notre Dame's 6-foot-9, 238-pound power forward, Dennis Latimore. Warrick pumped-faked in the lane, and, while flat-footed, leapt over the outstretched arms of Latimore and emphatically slammed the ball with one hand.{{cite web |title=Best dunk I've seen |first=Kim |last=Baxter |date=2006-01-11 |url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2006/01/best_dunk_ive_seen.html |work=The Post-Standard |access-date=2007-09-02}} In March 2023, Syracuse University officially retired his #1 jersey alongside his teammate [[Gerry McNamara]].{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Etan |author1-link=Etan Thomas |title=Hakim Warrick Q&A: 2003 Syracuse championship and jersey retirement |url=https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/hakim-warrick-qa-2003-syracuse-championship-and-jersey-retirement |access-date=8 March 2023 |work=www.basketballnews.com |date=3 March 2023 |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===NBA=== ====Memphis Grizzlies==== Warrick was projected as high as a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery pick]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]] or as low as a mid-first-round pick.{{cite web |title=Hakim Warrick Draft Capsule |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=2049800&prov=st&type=lgns |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130209203411/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=2049800&prov=st&type=lgns |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 9, 2013 |work=Yahoo! |access-date=2007-09-02 }} Although Warrick's 38-inch vertical jump and a 7–2 wingspan impressed NBA scouts, they often worried that he was not heavy enough to guard the stronger power forwards in the NBA and did not possess the ballhandling ability associated with small forward. Warrick ended up slipping to the 19th pick, where he was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web |title=Hakim Warrick |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/2005/draft/players/53.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071110073859/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/2005/draft/players/53.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 10, 2007 |work=SI.com |access-date=2007-09-02}} Warrick appeared in 68 games as a rookie, including two starts, and averaged 4.1 points and 2.1 assists in 10.6 minutes per game playing behind [[Pau Gasol]]. On January 31, 2006, Warrick was named to be one of the contestants in the NBA All-Star [[Slam Dunk Contest]] during the All-Star Weekend. He came in third place, behind [[New York Knicks]] guard [[Nate Robinson]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]] forward [[Andre Iguodala]].{{cite web |title=Hakim Warrick |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/hakim_warrick/bio.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=2007-09-02}} Warrick also played in three playoff games in his rookie season, as the Grizzlies were swept in four games by the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On April 29, 2006, Warrick scored 11 points, including 7-of-8 free throws in a 94–89 overtime loss.{{cite web |title=Mavericks 94, Grizzlies 89 OT |date=2006-04-29 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=260429029 |access-date=2007-09-29}} Warrick started Game Four in place of [[Jake Tsakalidis]].{{cite web |title=Mavericks 102, Grizzlies 76 |date=2006-05-01 |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/sports/nba/20060501-1953-bkn-mavericks-grizzlies.html |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-29}} Warrick finished the playoff series with averages of 6.7 points and 2.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=NBA.com Hakim Warrick Statistics |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/hakim_warrick/career_stats.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=2007-09-02}} Over the summer of 2006, Memphis lost their star forward Gasol to a broken foot, leaving Warrick as one of the team's top options as starting power forward. Warrick played in all 82 games in 2006–07, including 43 starts. On December 9, 2006, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Warrick recorded career highs in points (31) and rebounds (13) and made all nine of his [[free throw]] attempts in a 100–94 loss.{{cite web |title=Milwaukee 100, Memphis 94 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2006120815 |date=2006-12-08 |work=The Associated Press |access-date=2007-09-02}} He later set a new career high of 16 rebounds in the Grizzlies 116–111 loss to the Phoenix Suns. Warrick finished the season with averages of 12.7 points per game and 5.1 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. ====Later years==== On July 31, 2009, Warrick signed a one-year deal with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |date=2009-08-01 |title=Warrick agrees to 1-year deal with Bucks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4370954 |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} On February 18, 2010, Warrick was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] along with [[Joe Alexander (basketball)|Joe Alexander]] for [[John Salmons]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/salmons_trade_100218.html |title=Bulls deal Salmons to Bucks for Warrick and Alexander |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-02-18 |access-date=2010-02-18}} On July 8, 2010, Warrick agreed to a 4-year, $18 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2010_11/ |title=NBA Transactions 2010–11 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2010-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100707022018/http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2010_11/ |archive-date=2010-07-07 |url-status=dead }} The deal was completed as a sign-and-trade, which resulted in Phoenix giving up their 2011 second round pick to [[Chicago Bulls|Chicago]]. The pick was later acquired by the [[Golden State Warriors]], who used it to draft [[Charles Jenkins (basketball)|Charles Jenkins]]. Warrick started only 6 total games with the Suns. On July 27, 2012, Warrick was traded along with [[Robin Lopez]] to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in a three-way trade that included the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].[http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-lopez-and-warrick-phoenix HORNETS ACQUIRE LOPEZ AND WARRICK FROM PHOENIX] Warrick only played a grand total of 7 minutes with the Hornets.{{Cite web|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2012-11-13/hakim-warrick-matt-carroll-trade-charlotte-bobcats-new-orleans-hornets|title=NBA News, Scores, Videos, Standings and Schedule | Sporting News|access-date=2012-11-23|archive-date=2013-02-02|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130202165856/http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2012-11-13/hakim-warrick-matt-carroll-trade-charlotte-bobcats-new-orleans-hornets|url-status=dead}} On November 13, 2012, Warrick was traded to the Charlotte Bobcats for [[Matt Carroll (basketball)|Matt Carroll]].[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/bobcats-acquire-hakim-warrick-new-orleans-exchange-matt-carroll Bobcats trade Carroll for Warrick] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121116021157/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/bobcats-acquire-hakim-warrick-new-orleans-exchange-matt-carroll |date=2012-11-16 }} At the trade deadline on February 21, 2013, Warrick was traded to the Orlando Magic in exchange for [[Josh McRoberts]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/magic-acquire-harris-lamb-and-udrih-milwaukee-warrick-charlotte |title=Magic Acquire Harris, Lamb and Udrih From Milwaukee; Warrick from Charlotte|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=February 21, 2013 |access-date=March 30, 2013}} He never played for the Magic as he was waived by them two days later. ===Overseas=== ====China and Turkey==== In November 2013, Warrick worked out for the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA)[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/108279/hakim-warrick-is-working-out-in-china.html Hakim Warrick is working out in China] but was subsequently not signed. In December 2013, he signed with the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]], also of the CBA.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/109337/hakim-warrick-signs-in-china.html Hakim Warrick signs in China] On January 5, 2015, Warrick signed with [[Torku Konyaspor B.K.|Torku Konyaspor]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/147391/konyaspor-agreed-to-terms-with-former-nba-forward-hakim-warrick.html Konyaspor agreed to terms with former NBA forward Hakim Warrick] ====Australia==== [[File:Melbourne United team bench, December 2015.jpg|thumb|Warrick with Melbourne United in 2015]] On September 22, 2015, Warrick signed with [[Melbourne United]] for the [[2015–16 NBL season]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/featured-news/melbourne-signs-nba-veteran-hakim-warrick/ |title=MELBOURNE SIGNS NBA VETERAN HAKIM WARRICK |access-date=2015-09-22 |archive-date=2015-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925035615/http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/featured-news/melbourne-signs-nba-veteran-hakim-warrick/ |url-status=dead }} After averaging 12.8 points per game for United off the bench over the first five games, helping the team earn a 5–0 start, Warrick sustained a groin injury[https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/melbourne-united-lose-nba-import-hakim-warrick-for-perth-wildcats-sydney-kings-games-20151028-gkkmcv.html Melbourne United lose NBA import Hakim Warrick for Perth Wildcats, Sydney Kings games] and was placed on the short-term injury waiver list. He was temporarily replaced in the line-up by [[Garrett Jackson]] on October 29,{{Cite web |url=http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/featured-news/jackson-in-for-warrick/ |title=JACKSON IN FOR WARRICK |access-date=2015-10-29 |archive-date=2015-11-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101050534/http://www.melbourneutd.com.au/featured-news/jackson-in-for-warrick/ |url-status=dead }} returning from injury on November 22 to face the [[New Zealand Breakers]].{{cite web | last=Smart | first=Nick | title=Melbourne United welcomes back Hakim Warrick for New Zealand clash | website=Herald Sun| date=2015-11-21 | url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/basketball/melbourne-united-welcomes-back-hakim-warrick-for-new-zealand-clash/news-story/2c8d9bf3ed3a6d807f1c9ac212d5054d?nk=bf201fe81765f2e467c3b76a270f1e13-1729532806 | access-date=2024-10-21}} On February 17, 2016, he was named [[NBL Best Sixth Man Award|NBL Best Sixth Man]] for the 2015–16 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/nba-veteran-hakim-warrick-wins-best-sixth-man/ |title=NBA VETERAN HAKIM WARRICK WINS BEST SIXTH MAN |access-date=2016-02-17 |archive-date=2016-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160225042539/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/nba-veteran-hakim-warrick-wins-best-sixth-man/ |url-status=dead }} Warrick helped lead United to the minor premiership after finishing the regular season in first place on the ladder with an 18–10 win–loss record. However, in their semi-final series against the fourth-seeded [[New Zealand Breakers]], United were swept 2–0 to bow out of the playoffs.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/sf2-report-breakers-sweep-united-to-enter-grand-final/ |title=SF2 REPORT: BREAKERS SWEEP UNITED TO ENTER GRAND FINAL |access-date=2016-02-22 |archive-date=2016-02-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160223061003/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/sf2-report-breakers-sweep-united-to-enter-grand-final/ |url-status=dead }} In 23 games for United in 2015–16, Warrick averaged 14.2 points and 6.0 rebounds per game. ====Greece==== On February 24, 2016, Warrick signed to play in Greece, with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and [[Euroleague]], for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Olympiacos adds size with Warrick|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6pdygpnaehawtpoc/olympiacos-adds-size-with-warrick|access-date=February 24, 2016|work=Euroleague.net|date=February 24, 2016}} Olympiacos won the Greek Basket League championship in 2015–2016.[https://www.flashscore.com/basketball/greece/basket-league-2015-2016/standings/ Flashscore.com] 2015–2016 Greek Basket League standings. Retrieved January 17, 2020. ====Israel==== On April 28, 2018, Warrick signed with the Israeli team [[Ironi Nahariya]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|script-title=he:בא לעבוד: האקים ווריק מגיע
